astm-d638.title: ASTM D638-22 — Standard Test Method for Tensile Properties of Plastics
astm-d638.scope: Public scope and significance/use statements, not a reproduction of the full standard. This source does not establish that a supplier used D638 or complied with any particular procedure.

amza-2021.title: Accelerated Aging Effect on Mechanical Properties of Common 3D-Printing Polymers
amza-2021.scope: FFF specimens: opaque blue Fillamentum PLA Extrafill and transparent natural PrimaSelect PETG; Creality Ender-3, Cura 4.5, 100% grid ±45° infill, 0.2 mm layers, two contours. PLA nozzle/bed: 205/45 °C; PETG: 235/65 °C. Unaged controls are discussed separately from UV-B-aged groups; ASTM D638-14 Type I dimensions, 1 mm/min, 23 °C / 50% RH, five specimens per tensile group. Ultimate strength is distinct from the supplier yield property.

fischbach-2023.title: Effect of physical aging on the flexural creep in 3D printed thermoplastic
fischbach-2023.scope: Author manuscript, printed BASF Ultrafuse PLA; 100% infill, 0.2 mm layers, 215 °C nozzle, 30 °C bed; ISO 899-2 bending creep. The long-duration test uses one specimen under a 10 N nominal force for 170 h near 20 °C. No family-wide lifetime or reduction factor is inferred. The long-duration specimen had an initial age of five hours; the authors report laboratory relative humidity of 30–50%.

astm-d256.title: ASTM D256-26 — Standard Test Methods for Determining the Izod Pendulum Impact Resistance of Plastics
astm-d256.scope: Public scope and significance/use statements explain impact-test dependencies. No paid standard text or material-specific impact design value is reproduced.

stratasys-tooling.title: Design Considerations: FDM Additive Manufacturing Tooling
stratasys-tooling.scope: Industrial Stratasys FDM tooling guidance. It supplies design context, not qualification of the Prusament grades or a desktop printer. A precise publication date is not stated in the document metadata used here.

iso-75-1-2020.title: ISO 75-1:2020 — Plastics — Determination of temperature of deflection under load — Part 1: General test method
iso-75-1-2020.scope: Public abstract, not the paid full standard. Its method scope and limits explain HDT; it does not establish the edition used by the filament supplier.

iso-75-2-2013.title: ISO 75-2:2013 — Plastics — Determination of temperature of deflection under load — Part 2: Plastics and ebonite
iso-75-2-2013.scope: Public abstract identifies the method stresses. Exact publication day was not recorded; no day is invented.

astm-d648-18.title: ASTM D648-18 — Standard Test Method for Deflection Temperature of Plastics Under Flexural Load in the Edgewise Position
astm-d648-18.scope: Public scope and significance/use explain the limits of this test and its technical differences from ISO 75. This does not certify supplier compliance.

astm-d1525-25.title: ASTM D1525-25 — Standard Test Method for Vicat Softening Temperature of Plastics
astm-d1525-25.scope: Public scope identifies the controlled needle-penetration measurement. No full standard text or product-specific Vicat qualification is reproduced.

astm-e1356-25.title: ASTM E1356-25 — Standard Test Method for Assignment of the Glass Transition Temperatures by Differential Scanning Calorimetry
astm-e1356-25.scope: Public scope and significance/use explain the DSC heat-capacity transition, rather than a component load-bearing limit.

astm-e1640-23.title: ASTM E1640-23 — Standard Test Method for Assignment of the Glass Transition Temperature By Dynamic Mechanical Analysis
astm-e1640-23.scope: Public significance/use explains the viscoelastic transition, dependence on the measurement technique, and the ideal storage-modulus-onset interpretation.

polymaker-htpla-tds-v11.title: Polymaker HT-PLA Technical Data Sheet
polymaker-htpla-tds-v11.version: V1.1 in the linked PDF filename; no printed issue date identified
polymaker-htpla-tds-v11.scope: PDF thermal rows explicitly separate as-printed and annealed material. HDT geometry, orientation, conditioning, replicate count, heating rate and actual annealing schedule are not identified. The general specimen recipe and recommended anneal are not silently assigned to the HDT tests.

benwood-2018.title: Improving the Impact Strength and Heat Resistance of 3D Printed Models: Structure, Property, and Processing Correlationships during Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) of Poly(Lactic Acid)
benwood-2018.scope: True Red PolyLite PLA, 2.85 mm filament, Lulzbot Taz 6. The study combines printed and separately identified injection-molded specimens; only its printed-process observations inform this article. Its ASTM D648 experiment is kept separate from supplier ISO 75 results.

tensile-test-scope.locator: Public Significance and Use §§4.1, 4.3–4.5 and Note 5; Scope §1.1 and Note 1.
tensile-test-scope.finding: Tensile properties depend on specimen preparation, rate and environment; modulus characterizes the initial response. Testing over different load durations and environments is needed for engineering use. ASTM D638 and ISO 527-1 have differing technical content.

stiffness-vs-strength.locator: §2 and Table 1 (materials and printing); §3.2, Table 2, PLA Control and PETG Control columns.
stiffness-vs-strength.finding: In the unaged control groups, the tested PLA specimens had a higher modulus while the tested PETG specimens had a higher ultimate tensile strength. This is an independent printed-grade result, not a yield-stress comparison or a statement about all PLA and PETG.

direction-and-load-path.finding: The guide connects FDM orientation to directional strength and recommends a short, direct load path. Its process-specific statements are not universal Z-strength data.

prusa-orientation.locator: Archive member Prusament PLA/1_PLA_Prusament_TDS_2022_EN.pdf, PDF p. 3, orientation sketch; corresponding PDF p. 3 sketches in PETG, ASA and PC Blend sheets.
prusa-orientation.finding: The inspected source sketches show both tensile coupons with the long axis along X: Horizontal is flat XY, and Vertical xz is on-edge XZ. Those are not in-plane versus build-Z tensile tests. The corresponding series retain their own source locators.

creep-below-tg.finding: One printed Ultrafuse PLA specimen continued to creep under the long room-temperature bending hold below its glass transition. This evidence calls for a sustained-load check but does not supply a general lifetime prediction.

impact-test-scope.locator: Public Scope §1.1 and Notes 3–4; Significance and Use §§5.2, 5.7–5.9.
impact-test-scope.finding: Specimen preparation, notch, conditioning and failure type affect impact results. A no-break observation is not an unlimited impact resistance. Results from different impact methods and specimen configurations do not establish a common ranking.

industrial-tooling-context.locator: §1.4, printed p. 4, Volvo Trucks application context.
industrial-tooling-context.finding: The manufacturer documents industrial FDM use by Volvo Trucks for lifting devices and ancillary tooling. This passage does not identify the exact grade or load rating for each component.

hdt-is-load-and-time-specific.finding: ISO 75 uses a heated three-point-bending test under defined stress. Its result does not establish maximum use temperature, design performance or long-term endurance.

hdt-two-stresses.locator: Public Abstract, methods A and B.
hdt-two-stresses.finding: ISO 75-2 identifies 1.80 MPa for method A and 0.45 MPa for method B. They are different test stresses, not interchangeable HDT labels.

d648-is-not-iso75.locator: Public Significance and Use §5.1; Scope Note 3.
d648-is-not-iso75.finding: ASTM D648 limits extrapolation to other exposure conditions and says its results must not be compared with ISO 75-1/-2 results because their technical content differs.

vicat-is-penetration.finding: Vicat identifies a specified needle-penetration response during controlled heating, rather than the flexural deflection measured by HDT.

tg-by-dsc.finding: DSC assigns a glass-transition temperature from a heat-capacity step in the material’s amorphous region.

tg-by-dma.finding: DMA examines temperature- and frequency-dependent viscoelastic response. The glass transition spans a range; the reported assigned temperature depends on the technique.

annealing-changes-printed-pla.locator: Experimental Section: Materials, Fused Deposition Modeling, Annealing and Thermal Analysis; Results: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis and Heat Deflection Temperature Changes, Figures 13–14.
annealing-changes-printed-pla.finding: The printed True Red PolyLite PLA study links thermal history, crystallinity and HDT. Its separately specified annealed specimens are not the HT-PLA grade or a transferable annealing recipe.

htpla-annealing-protocol-gap.locator: PDF p. 3, Thermal Properties; PDF p. 5, annealing note; PDF p. 6, How to Make Specimens.
htpla-annealing-protocol-gap.finding: The table labels annealed results; the recommendation and general recipe are separate from an identified HDT specimen protocol.

prusa-thermal-basis-gap.locator: PDF p. 2, Typical material properties HDT rows, compared with the separate Mechanical properties of 3D printed testing specimens table and its footnote (3) on p. 3.
prusa-thermal-basis-gap.finding: The PC Blend sheet’s thermal rows are outside the explicitly printed mechanical table. Its tensile-coupon orientation and recipe are not established thermal-test conditions.

composite-pa6-axes.locator: Property-table footnote immediately before the FAQ.
composite-pa6-axes.finding: The supplier describes Z as layer-to-layer behavior. The linked TDS retains the XY/Z labels but does not document its Z specimen preparation. Store numerical units and FAQ conditioning numbers are not used.

composite-pa6-protocol.locator: PDF p. 1, dry/wet mechanical-table footnotes, specimen-printing settings and note above them.
composite-pa6-protocol.finding: Both mechanical groups were annealed at 100 °C for 16 h. The wet group subsequently underwent 48 h immersion in 60 °C water. Filament drying is a separate recommendation; actual dry-group residual moisture and test temperature are not specified.

composite-pa12-axes.locator: Property-table footnote immediately before the FAQ.
composite-pa12-axes.finding: The supplier describes Z as layer-to-layer behavior. The linked TDS retains the XY/Z labels but does not document its Z specimen preparation. Store numerical units and FAQ conditioning numbers are not used.

composite-pa12-protocol.locator: PDF p. 1, dry/wet mechanical-table footnotes, specimen-printing settings and note above them.
composite-pa12-protocol.finding: Both mechanical groups were annealed at 100 °C for 16 h. The wet group subsequently underwent 48 h immersion in 60 °C water. Filament drying is a separate recommendation; actual dry-group residual moisture and test temperature are not specified.

composite-pa12-formulation.locator: Product description under Professional-Grade Mechanical Strength and Dimensional Stability.
composite-pa12-formulation.finding: The manufacturer markets the material as a PA12-based long-chain copolyamide containing 10% carbon fiber. The TDS has inconsistent matrix terminology; no exact comonomer recipe is established.

composite-pccf-scope.locator: PDF p. 2 lower mechanical table and p. 3 specimen printing note/orientation drawing.
composite-pccf-scope.finding: The PC-based composite has yield and tensile-modulus measurements on flat and on-edge coupons. Both have length along X. Its mechanical rows provide neither true build-Z tension nor a matched moisture-conditioned dataset.

composite-pa12-annealing-discrepancy.locator: FAQ asking whether prints require annealing; compare V1.1 TDS p. 1 dry/wet footnotes.
composite-pa12-annealing-discrepancy.finding: The product-page FAQ recommends a ten-hour anneal whereas the mechanical-table footnotes state sixteen hours. This article follows the footnotes attached to the measured specimens.

composite-cure-application.locator: Why these Specific Polymaker Materials; final Example Components image captions.
composite-cure-application.finding: The manufacturer identifies Fiberon PA6-CF20 in CURE Mannheim steering hardware and aerodynamic cores produced by filament printing. No loads, validation margins or conditioning history are supplied, so this example cannot qualify another design.

composite-pa6-formulation.locator: Product description under Engineered for Demanding Applications.
composite-pa6-formulation.finding: The manufacturer identifies a PA6 matrix with a marketed 20% carbon-fiber fraction. The inspected description does not state the mass-versus-volume basis or fiber dimensions.
